import MumfordLib.GroupCohomologyCupOne

/-!
# Bilinear integral group two-cocycles

An additive bilinear map on an abelian group is an inhomogeneous group
two-cocycle with trivial integral coefficients.  This is the concrete
producer behind the character cup cocycles and will be used when assembling
finite-free alternating forms from decomposable terms.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

namespace Mumford.Analytic

variable {U : Type} [AddCommGroup U]

/-- The inhomogeneous cocycle associated to an integral bilinear map. -/
def groupBilinearCocycle (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupCohomology.cocycles₂ (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ) := by
  refine ⟨fun p => B p.1.toAdd p.2.toAdd, ?_⟩
  apply (groupCohomology.mem_cocycles₂_iff _).mpr
  intro x y z
  change B (x.toAdd + y.toAdd) z.toAdd + B x.toAdd y.toAdd =
    B y.toAdd z.toAdd + B x.toAdd (y.toAdd + z.toAdd)
  simp only [map_add, AddMonoidHom.add_apply]
  abel

@[simp]
theorem groupBilinearCocycle_apply (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) (u v : U) :
    groupBilinearCocycle B (Multiplicative.ofAdd u, Multiplicative.ofAdd v) =
      B u v := rfl

@[simp]
theorem groupBilinearCocycle_add (B C : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupBilinearCocycle (B + C) =
      groupBilinearCocycle B + groupBilinearCocycle C := by
  ext p
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem groupBilinearCocycle_smul (c : ℤ) (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupBilinearCocycle (c • B) = c • groupBilinearCocycle B := by
  ext p
  rfl

/-! The cocycle constructor is linear before passing to cohomology. -/

/-- Bilinear maps assemble linearly into integral group two-cocycles. -/
def groupBilinearCocycleLinear :
    (U →+ U →+ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ]
      groupCohomology.cocycles₂ (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ) where
  toFun := groupBilinearCocycle
  map_add' := groupBilinearCocycle_add
  map_smul' := groupBilinearCocycle_smul

@[simp]
theorem groupBilinearCocycleLinear_apply (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupBilinearCocycleLinear B = groupBilinearCocycle B := rfl

/-- The degree-two class represented by a bilinear cocycle. -/
def groupBilinearClass (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupCohomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ) :=
  groupCohomology.H2π _ (groupBilinearCocycle B)

/-- Bilinear cocycles assemble linearly into actual second group cohomology.

This packages the additivity of the inhomogeneous bilinear cocycle construction
for later finite-free decompositions of alternating forms. -/
def groupBilinearClassLinear :
    (U →+ U →+ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ]
      groupCohomology.H2 (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ) where
  toFun := groupBilinearClass
  map_add' B C := by
    change (groupCohomology.H2π (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ)).hom
        (groupBilinearCocycle (B + C)) =
      (groupCohomology.H2π (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ)).hom
          (groupBilinearCocycle B) +
        (groupCohomology.H2π (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ)).hom
          (groupBilinearCocycle C)
    rw [groupBilinearCocycle_add]
    exact (groupCohomology.H2π (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ)).hom.map_add _ _
  map_smul' c B := by
    rw [groupBilinearClass, groupBilinearClass]
    rw [groupBilinearCocycle_smul]
    exact (groupCohomology.H2π (Rep.trivial ℤ (Multiplicative U) ℤ)).hom.map_smul c _

@[simp]
theorem groupBilinearClassLinear_apply (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupBilinearClassLinear B = groupBilinearClass B := rfl

/-- Alternation of a bilinear group cocycle is its skew-symmetrization. -/
@[simp]
theorem groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass
    (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) (v : Fin 2 → U) :
    groupSecondCohomologyAlternation (groupBilinearClass B) v =
      B (v 0) (v 1) - B (v 1) (v 0) := by
  rw [groupBilinearClass, groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_π]
  rfl

/-- The skew-symmetrization of an integral bilinear form, viewed as an
alternating map.  Defining it by composition makes the factorization through
actual group cohomology explicit. -/
def groupBilinearAlternation :
    (U →+ U →+ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] AlternatingMap ℤ U ℤ (Fin 2) :=
  (groupSecondCohomologyAlternation (U := U)).comp groupBilinearClassLinear

@[simp]
theorem groupBilinearAlternation_apply (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) (v : Fin 2 → U) :
    groupBilinearAlternation B v = B (v 0) (v 1) - B (v 1) (v 0) := by
  change groupSecondCohomologyAlternation (groupBilinearClassLinear B) v = _
  rw [groupBilinearClassLinear_apply]
  exact groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass B v

/-- Alternation of the bilinear-class map is exactly bilinear
skew-symmetrization. -/
theorem groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_comp_groupBilinearClassLinear :
    (groupSecondCohomologyAlternation (U := U)).comp groupBilinearClassLinear =
      groupBilinearAlternation := by
  rfl

/-- A symmetric bilinear cocycle has trivial alternation. -/
@[simp]
theorem groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass_of_symmetric
    (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) (hB : ∀ u v, B u v = B v u) :
    groupSecondCohomologyAlternation (groupBilinearClass B) = 0 := by
  ext v
  rw [groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass]
  rw [hB]
  simp

/- The antisymmetric case records the integral factor arising from
   skew-symmetrization: `B u v - B v u = 2 * B u v`. -/
@[simp]
theorem groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass_of_antisymmetric
    (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) (hB : ∀ u v, B v u = -B u v) (v : Fin 2 → U) :
    groupSecondCohomologyAlternation (groupBilinearClass B) v =
      2 * B (v 0) (v 1) := by
  rw [groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass, hB]
  ring

theorem groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass_eq_zero_iff
    (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupSecondCohomologyAlternation (groupBilinearClass B) = 0 ↔
      ∀ u v, B u v = B v u := by
  constructor
  · intro h u v
    have hv := congrArg (fun F : AlternatingMap ℤ U ℤ (Fin 2) => F ![u, v]) h
    have hz : B u v - B v u = 0 := by
      simpa [groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass] using hv
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp hz
  · exact groupSecondCohomologyAlternation_groupBilinearClass_of_symmetric B

/-- Equality of bilinear alternations is exactly equality of their
skew-symmetrizations.  This is the two-cocycle kernel criterion in the
bilinear presentation, and is convenient when comparing decompositions. -/
theorem groupBilinearAlternation_eq_iff
    (B C : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupBilinearAlternation B = groupBilinearAlternation C ↔
      ∀ u v, B u v - B v u = C u v - C v u := by
  constructor
  · intro h u v
    have hv := congrArg (fun F : AlternatingMap ℤ U ℤ (Fin 2) => F ![u, v]) h
    simpa [groupBilinearAlternation_apply] using hv
  · intro h
    ext w
    simpa [groupBilinearAlternation_apply] using h (w 0) (w 1)

/-- The bilinear alternation vanishes precisely on symmetric bilinear maps.
This is the map-level kernel statement obtained from the equality criterion. -/
theorem groupBilinearAlternation_eq_zero_iff
    (B : U →+ U →+ ℤ) :
    groupBilinearAlternation B = 0 ↔ ∀ u v, B u v = B v u := by
  constructor
  · intro h u v
    have hskew := (groupBilinearAlternation_eq_iff B 0).mp (by simpa using h) u v
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp (by simpa using hskew)
  · intro h
    have hz : groupBilinearAlternation B =
        groupBilinearAlternation (0 : U →+ U →+ ℤ) := by
      apply (groupBilinearAlternation_eq_iff B 0).mpr
      intro u v
      simp [h u v]
    simpa using hz

end Mumford.Analytic
